approach: Add Priority::Urgent as the first (best) variant. Add a new `athena.priority/1` record (job, sequence n, level, why, time) at `<job dir>/priority-<n>.json`, loaded into JobRecords; the highest n wins. Add `Athena::set_priority` (in reading.rs) and a CLI command `athena priority <job> <level> --why ...` that checks the level, finds the job, requires it to be queued, and commits one new record. One function in reading.rs, `job_priority(job)`, gives the priority from the newest record, else urgent if the latest reading carries an `urgent_reason`, else the `Priority:` line in the text. `plan_entry` and `status::job_line` both call it, so `athena plan` and `athena status` agree. The reader marks urgency with a new `ReadingOutput.urgent_reason: Option<String>`, a hardened required property. Its field doc in outputs.rs holds the rule, so reader.md is not edited. The Reading record gains an optional `urgent_reason` that old records still parse without. Tests cover the ordering, the override (including through the real command on a fixture repo), and the reading. CHANGELOG.md and docs/decisions.md get entries.

decisions.choice: A new append-only record kind `athena.priority/1`, one file per record, `<job dir>/priority-<n>.json`; the highest n wins.
decisions.reason: Requests stay append-only. It follows how corrections are stored (`correction-<n>.json`). Highest n gives a deterministic latest-wins that does not depend on timestamps, and it keeps history. Re-prioritising needs no re-queue.

rejected.option: Rewrite the Priority line in request.json
rejected.why: Breaks the append-only rule and is out of scope.
A record per job is how all job data is stored, and the schema registry then validates it.
Equal or skewed clocks make it non-deterministic. The existing scores use the timestamp, but a sequence number is safer.

decisions.choice: The priority record stores the level as a string (urgent/high/normal/low), validated in AnyRecord::parse and again in the command. Conversion to `plan::Priority` happens in core.
decisions.reason: athena-data cannot depend on athena-core, where `Priority` lives. A validated string avoids moving the enum between crates.

rejected.why: A wider refactor touching the status, display and drain callers, for no gain.

decisions.choice: The reader marks urgency through a new required nullable field `urgent_reason` in ReadingOutput. The rule is its field doc, which goes into the generated schema. A non-empty reason means urgent. reader.md is not changed.
decisions.reason: reader.md is at 1997 of 2000 tokens. Requiring the field makes the reader answer it every time. Requiring a reason keeps the record auditable. The field doc is the only place the rule lives.

rejected.why: It would exceed the budget, and the user chose outputs.rs or briefs.rs.
The request requires the reason to be recorded in the reading.
Brittle. The reader's judgement is the intended mechanism.

decisions.choice: Precedence in `job_priority`: the newest priority record, else Urgent if the latest reading has an urgent_reason, else the text's Priority line. The record overrides everything, including the reader's urgency.
decisions.reason: The operator's explicit later choice should beat both automatic sources. This also lets the operator demote a wrongly urgent request.

rejected.why: It would make demotion impossible, which contradicts 'overriding'.

decisions.choice: The command takes only queued jobs (JobState::Queued) and rejects unknown ids and unknown levels with a clear error before writing anything.
decisions.reason: Matches the request and criterion 4. Queued jobs are what plan orders, and the check gives a clear error instead of a silent no-op.

rejected.why: It was explicitly scoped to queued requests.

decisions.choice: The Reading record's new field is `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] urgent_reason: Option<String>`.
decisions.reason: Existing committed readings have no such key and the struct denies unknown fields, so old records must still parse. None-valued fields stay out of the JSON, so ordinary readings serialise as before.

rejected.why: It would invalidate every existing reading record.

risks.risk: The new required ReadingOutput field breaks fixtures and fake agents that emit reader JSON without it.
risks.mitigation: Add `"urgent_reason": null` to the listed fixtures. Run the full cargo test early, after the field is added.

risks.risk: The field doc and the new required property push the reader set over its 2000-token budget, if the schema is counted.
risks.mitigation: Keep the doc short (about 60 words). Run the budgets test right after the edit. If it fails, trim the doc, not reader.md.

risks.risk: Adding a field to Reading breaks parsing of old committed records or the record gate.
risks.mitigation: serde default plus skip_serializing_if. Add a test that parses a reading JSON without the key and round-trips one with it.

risks.risk: store.rs is outside the brief's file list, and a wide change there could conflict with other jobs.
risks.mitigation: The change is two small additions (one field, one match arm). It is stated in the plan, and there is no other way to load the record.

risks.risk: The existing from_text test and display tests assert 'urgent' gives Normal, or match Priority exhaustively.
risks.mitigation: Update the plan.rs assertion. The compiler flags non-exhaustive matches, and display.rs uses only as_str and a Normal comparison.

risks.risk: Two priority commands racing could write the same n.
risks.mitigation: Take the job lock as close_with does, and write n = max + 1 against the head's records. A collision fails at commit instead of overwriting.

demonstrations.method: A unit test in plan.rs builds entries with Urgent, High, Normal and Low priorities and a dependency chain. It asserts the order urgent < high < normal < low, and that an urgent dependent still comes after its low-priority prerequisite. Because the prerequisite inherits the urgent dependent's priority, it also comes before unrelated high items. It also asserts `Priority::Urgent < Priority::High`.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes, showing the order urgent, high, normal, low, and the dependency before its urgent dependent.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the Urgent variant sorted before High, the urgent entry would not come first, or the test would not compile. Without the dependency rule, the urgent dependent would precede its prerequisite.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in reading.rs: a job whose text says `Priority: normal` plus a priority record of urgent. Assert that `plan_entry(...).priority` is Urgent, that Plan::build puts it before an older high item, that the status line's priority (`status::job_line`) is Urgent, and that the request is unchanged. A CLI integration test in crates/athena-cli/tests/priority.rs uses the Fixture to queue two requests with `ask --later`, then reads the plan order and status. It runs set_priority (the same function the command calls), reads them again, and asserts the order and status changed. It also checks that exactly one new `priority-1.json` file was added, request.json is byte-identical, and an unknown level or a non-queued or unknown job errors.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-core priority && cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test priority
demonstrations.observes: Plan order and the status priority flip after the record, with no new or changed request record. Errors name the bad level or job.
demonstrations.fails_without: If plan_entry or job_line ignored the record, the order and status would not change. If the command rewrote the request, the byte-identity check would fail.

demonstrations.method: Reading tests. (a) A reading with `urgent_reason: Some("cuts retries that redo work")` gives `plan_entry(...).priority == Urgent`, and the reason is on the Reading. (b) A reading with None, for an ordinary request, is not urgent. (c) The parse path (the function around reading.rs:385) takes a ReadingOutput JSON with a reason and one with null, and checks the recorded `urgent_reason` is redacted-and-kept or None. A blank reason counts as None. (d) The schema from `reading_schema` lists `urgent_reason` as required, with the rule in its description (an outputs.rs test).
demonstrations.observes: The speed request comes out Urgent with its reason recorded, and the ordinary one does not.
demonstrations.fails_without: If urgent_reason were not carried from the output into the record, or not used by plan_entry, test (a) would find a Normal priority.

demonstrations.method: Tests: `Priority::from_text("Priority: urgent") == Urgent` (the old assertion at plan.rs:644 expecting Normal is updated). The command's tests cover an unknown level, an unknown job id, and a non-queued job (a read job), each failing with a message and writing nothing. A valid call appends only a `priority-<n>.json`. A clap parse test or the existing help test checks that the help text names urgent and the command.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-core plan:: && cargo test --locked -p athena-cli
demonstrations.observes: from_text parses urgent. The error cases fail with clear messages. The help contains 'urgent' and 'priority'.
demonstrations.fails_without: None of the error cases would be rejected without the validation, and from_text would still return Normal for 'urgent'.

demonstrations.method: A test in outputs.rs asserts that the generated reading schema's `urgent_reason` description contains the rule terms (faster, wasted time, failed or rejected attempts, planning stops, timeouts, retries, thrash, duplicated checks, reason). `git diff` shows reader.md unchanged, or only shorter if text was removed.
demonstrations.observes: The outputs.rs doc holds the rule. reader.md does not appear in the diff, or has fewer lines.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the rule were missing from the field doc, the schema test would fail.

demonstrations.method: Run the existing budgets test. The reader set (prompt, defaults, and so on) must stay within 2000 tokens. reader.md is untouched.
demonstrations.observes: every_role_set_is_within_its_budget passes. The reader count is at or below the budget.
demonstrations.fails_without: If reader.md grew, the test would fail by exceeding the budget.

demonstrations.method: Inspect the new CHANGELOG.md entry (urgent level, priority command, reader urgent_reason, record kind). Inspect the new docs/decisions.md decision with its alternatives. Both are written in the prevailing house style. Also check docs/records.md lists `athena.priority/1`.

demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
